identity: Novelist and social critic · United Kingdom · 1812–1870
title: Charles Dickens's birth chart
metaDescription: Charles Dickens's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 17.6° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Across the ten placements whose signs are settled, mutable leads with five. Mutable signs end their seasons, and a mutable-heavy chart is read as one built for adaptation and hand-off rather than for standing still.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun's position resolves to 17.6° Aquarius — deep enough in the second decan (10°–20°) that Mercury, its traditional sub-ruler, colours the reading.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 21.8° Capricorn, Venus was at 15.9° Pisces, Mars was at 7.3° Aries. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that works by atmosphere; effort spent in bursts and openings.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — Venus conjunction Pluto, 1.2° of separation. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Mercury sextile Uranus at 1.4°, and Venus square Neptune at 2.9° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: No closed figure — no grand trine, t-square, or grand cross — holds among the day-stable angles. The chart distributes its tension pair by pair rather than through one standing structure.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags five placements in this chart. The Sun in Aquarius at 17.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Venus in Pisces at 15.9° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Aries at 7.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Jupiter in Gemini at 26.5° is in detriment; Saturn in Capricorn at 4.3° is in domicile. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 3 fire, 3 water, 2 air, 2 earth by element and 5 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. A fire emphasis is read as appetite for the first move, with information gathered by doing rather than before doing. Jupiter was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Sagittarius for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.9° between midnight and midnight. The missing clock moves the Moon by half a sign at most here, and the boundary was never close. At the noon reference it stands at 8.4°.
